projects.description:
The proposed readiness project in the Republic of Kazakhstan addresses the urgent need to enhance resilience against the impacts of climate change. Recognizing the President's call for action, the Government supports the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) processes to integrate climate adaptation into policies, especially related to NDC implementation and decarbonization.
Focused on four priority sectors—agriculture, forestry, water management, and civil protection/disaster risk reduction – the project aims to establish clear mandates, coordination mechanisms, and standard procedures for climate adaptation at both national and sub-national levels. It seeks to provide decision-makers with climate services, enabling a comprehensive understanding of climate impacts and adaptation options. The project also aims to empower experts in the identified sectors to integrate climate risks into standard planning and budgeting procedures. Objectives include strengthening governance and institutional coordination, producing evidence for impactful adaptation solutions, catalyzing private sector engagement, and increasing adaptation finance. Emphasis will be placed on utilizing existing planning and budgeting processes for sustainable funding. Beneficiaries encompass key government ministries, decision-makers at various levels, business planners, and climate and sectoral experts, including women and vulnerable groups, contributing to a climate-resilient development pathway.

projects.name: Flood Control Using Integrated Dam Management System
projects.description:
The flood situation in 2024 was an unprecedented event. Frozen soil, sudden temperature rise and rainfall in conjunction with a considerable snow layer resulted in extremely high flows in the north and west of Kazakhstan. Many rivers experienced all-time high water levels and flood defence structures could not cope with the extreme flood volumes. The flood inundated large areas including settlements and agricultural zones and Aktobe was one of the hardest-hit cities in Kazakhstan.
This unprecedented flood revealed that preparedness, as part of efficient flood management, was not developed as it was supposed to be. The flood early warning systems to provide sufficient lead time did not exist. Specifically, dams did not have early warning systems which means preparation and foresighted flood operation are either not in place or just based on estimations and experiences of dam operators. However, the operators lack experience in addressing the increase in flow intensity, flow variability and speed floods developed in recent years due to climate change.
All in all, dams need urgent modernization in terms of three pillars: (1) Dam integrity; (2) Monitoring and dam surveillance; (3) Operation to enhance the flood management strategy in Kazakhstan, protect downstream riparians and ensure the full potential of flood attenuation of dams. Therefore, dams must be embedded into the national flood management concept of Kazakhstan as best as possible requiring the enhancement of early warning, dam monitoring, the rehabilitation of outdated structures and an update of operation rules.
The project aims to enhance flood resilience in Kazakhstan by strengthening dam safety and flood preparedness, directly supporting the disaster risk reduction and water priority sectors outlined in Kazakhstan's updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC). The updated NDC includes a dedicated chapter on climate change adaptation, emphasizing the importance of water resources management and disaster risk reduction as national adaptation priorities. This project aligns with these goals by improving infrastructure and preparedness measures to mitigate flood risks. Additionally, it complements the UNDP's ongoing initiative to integrate national adaptation plans into regional development strategies, ensuring a unified and comprehensive approach to climate resilience and sustainable development throughout Kazakhstan.

projects.name: Climate Promise Kazakhstan – From Pledge to Impact
projects.description:
This Project is part of the global UNDP’s flagship initiative, the Climate Promise: From Pledge to Impact - Leveraging the Climate Promise to turn enhanced Nationally Determined Contributions (eNDC) into ambitious climate action.
The project has been initiated as a response to the country's request for NDC Partnership. This project aims to support national efforts to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060, aligning with commitments such as the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and the Carbon Neutral Strategy. It involves developing a comprehensive tool and methodology to evaluate the impact of national programs and policies on GHG emissions, as well as building capacity among stakeholders to effectively use these tools.
The project also focuses on establishing measurable emission reduction outcomes, including long-term targets and interim milestones for key sectors. Sector-specific reduction pathways will be developed based on projections and scenarios, identifying programs and projects that can contribute to emissions reduction. Additionally, the project includes a social and gender impact assessment of the Carbon Neutral Strategy to ensure an equitable transition, along with the development of legislation and regulations to strengthen waste management practices and reduce sectoral emissions.

projects.name: Biodiversity finance initiative – BIOFIN, Extended Phase II
projects.description: BIOFIN supports countries with a methodology that provides innovative steps to measure current biodiversity expenditures, assess financial needs, identify the most suitable finance solutions, and provides guidance on how to implement these solutions to achieve their national biodiversity target. The 2nd phase of BIOFIN in Kazakhstan will be built on the lessons learned from the 1st phase and will aim to test six finance solutions: (1) subsidizing game breeding, (2) creating a basis for certification in the field of ecotourism, (3) capacity building of protected areas to improve financing, (4) biodiversity offsets, (5) carbon offsetting through an internal emission trading system (ETS) and (6) attracting foreign investment to implement projects to absorb greenhouse gases by forest ecosystems. The Phase II aims to establish the institutional and legal basis that will allow mobilizing financial resources for biodiversity through new financial solutions. Implementation of new finance solutions will be based on changing existing and preparing new legal standards, testing, studying the experience of other countries, approaches, capacity building of industry experts, providing extensive information on the problems and possibilities of biodiversity financing. The project also aims to highlight the key role of women in the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity, as well as the need for the full involvement of women at all levels of decision-making by mainstreaming gender issues into new financial decisions.

projects.name: Capacity Development of Public Servants for Advancing Digital Transformation and Digital Governance.
projects.description:
This project covers twelve countries situated in three geographical regions, i.e., in the Caucasus, and in Asia and the Pacific, which have taken some steps towards the digitalisation of their government operations and processes and for the delivery of public services to business and citizens, however in a varying degree. Moreover, most of them have also embraced the notion of digital transformation and of digital governance in their development strategies, although much still needs to be done towards their goal for digital transformation; incorporating the latest digital technologies, i.e., evidence-based policy formulation and implementation by harnessing abundant “big data”, or for the provision of proactive, efficient, and effective public services digitally.
Hence, this project – fully recognising the value of digital transformation and of digital governance – aims at further developing the capacities of public servants at different levels of government by transferring knowledge and experience enabling them to implement initiatives that will advance digital transformation and digital governance in their countries. It is expected that such knowledge and experience sharing will assist the participating countries to further develop policies initiatives that will allow them to establish data-driven public sectors for evidence-based policy making and implementation, and to introduce digital open governments that are proactive and user-driven resulting to efficient and effective public service provision and an increase of trust in government. As part of a working group on formulating the Migration Policy for 2023-27 and Social Code, UNHCR supported the Government by providing its technical expertise and recommendations for development of a Migration Policy for 2023-2027 and Social Code to enhance the national legal framework on asylum, refugee integration, extending their socio-economic rights including access to social protection services and allowance and facilitating naturalization. Bilateral meetings were conducted with line Ministries (MLSP, MoH, MoJ, MoEd), Members of the Parliament, Human Rights Ombudsman and other stakeholders, where the current situation of refugees, asylum-seekers and stateless persons in Kazakhstan, existing gaps in national legislation which hinder them from having effective access to social protection, employment, healthcare, education services, and necessary actions to be taken by the Government to promote and ensure the full realization of all human rights for all persons without discrimination in order to meet Kazakhstan’s obligations under international conventions were discussed. UNHCR recommendations were reflected in the Kazakhstan’s Human Rights action plan for 2022-2024. 
The refugee components were included in the 2nd Voluntary National Review (VNR) under SDG 10 “Granting access to basic socio-economic rights to refugees and asylum-seekers on an equal basis with permanently residing foreigners during their stay in Kazakhstan” and under SDG 16 “Ensuring the protection of the rights and interests of refugee and stateless children, ensuring security and access to social and educational services”. 

The situation of refugees in Kazakhstan along with challenges faced by them were submitted in the framework of UN Human Rights commissions (CERD and CAT) with recommendations to the Government of Kazakhstan to facilitate socio-economic integration and naturalization of refugees in line with international standards.

projects.name: Establishing HIV-1 Recent Infection Surveillance among Persons Newly Diagnosed with HIV Infection in KZ
projects.description:
GAM Report.  The UNAIDS office provided crucial technical assistance to Kazakhstan, supporting the timely submission of 80 key indicators for the Global AIDS Monitoring Reports. They enhanced the capabilities of 50 epidemiologists and 20 lab specialists across 20 AIDS Centers, improving their capacity to track progress toward the 95-95-95 targets. This effort aligns with Kazakhstan's commitment to the UN Political Declaration to end AIDS by 2030, showcasing tangible progress and contributing to the global fight against HIV/AIDS. 
Establishing HIV-1 Recent Infection Surveillance among Persons Newly Diagnosed with HIV Infection in Kazakhstan. The UNAIDS office played a pivotal role in aiding the Kazakh Scientific Center for Dermatology and Infection Diseases, under the Ministry of Health of Kazakhstan in enhancing the capabilities of staff across 20 AIDS regional centers in Kazakhstan. The focus was on implementing HIV Recency testing, an innovative methodology crucial for identifying recent HIV infections and tracing potential routes of transmission. Recent infections are more prevalent among urban residents (21%), with sex workers (25%) and men who have sex with men (22%) showing the highest proportions among key populations. A training workshop equipped 40 specialists from 20 regional and city HIV prevention centers to utilize the Spectrum program for subnational data preparation. Preliminary evaluation data from 20 centers were processed in Spectrum programme. Insights from these efforts are instrumental in translating data into impactful HIV prevention actions. Three Technical Working Group meetings conducted involving the AIDS service NGOs, community of People Living with HIV, and national/international organizations, focusing on the 2023-2026 HIV Roadmap. Also, staff members from the Kazakhstan Scientific Centre of Dermatology and Infectious Diseases contributed to the Regional HIV Assessment Workshop in Chisinau, Moldova, held from February 27 to March 3.

projects.name: Provide expert support and technical assistance to support  implementation of 2021 Global AIDS Strategy and HLM and integrate the new Strategy vision and targets  into the National Roadmap to eliminate AIDS in Kazakhstan by 2030.
projects.description:
The UNAIDS office played a pivotal role in March 2023 by providing crucial technical support to the Kazakh National Center for Dermatology and Infection Diseases. This support was instrumental in the development of the approved HIV Road Map 2023-2026, which currently functions as a guiding document, effectively coordinating national efforts in HIV prevention and treatment.

As Kazakhstan endeavors to achieve the ambitious goal of eliminating AIDS as a public health threat by 2030, it becomes imperative to proactively plan for the continuation of HIV response achievements beyond the year 2025. To sustain these efforts and ensure adequate financial resources, Kazakhstan should prioritize the creation of Sustainability Roadmaps for the HIV Response within the next two years. This strategic planning will be crucial in maintaining momentum and ensuring a robust, enduring response to the HIV epidemic.

Teamed up with UNDP/CCM Secretariat to organize a webinar series, providing valuable insights on applying for Global Fund Fighting AIDS, TB, and Malaria funding for 2023-2025. Engaged approximately 100 participants from AIDS service NGOs and the People Living with HIV community. Also, UNAIDS together with partners assisted the Kazakh Scientific Center for Dermatology and Infection Disease in formulating a funding proposal for the Global Fund Fighting AIDS, TB, and Malaria (GFATM). Successfully secured $7,422,991US for 2023-2025 to combat HIV and AIDS at country level.

projects.name: Phase 1. Climate Promise Kazakhstan – From Pledge to Impact
projects.description:
This Project Initiation Plan is part of the global UNDP’s flagship initiative, the Climate Promise: From Pledge to Impact - Leveraging the Climate Promise to turn enhanced Nationally Determined Contributions (eNDC) into ambitious climate action.
The project has been initiated as a response to the country's request for NDC Partnership. This project aims to support national efforts to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060, aligning with commitments such as the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and the Carbon Neutral Strategy. It involves developing a comprehensive tool and methodology to evaluate the impact of national programs and policies on GHG emissions, as well as building capacity among stakeholders to effectively use these tools.
The project also focuses on establishing measurable emission reduction outcomes, including long-term targets and interim milestones for key sectors. Sector-specific reduction pathways will be developed based on projections and scenarios, identifying programs and projects that can contribute to emissions reduction. Additionally, the project includes a social and gender impact assessment of the Carbon Neutral Strategy to ensure an equitable transition, along with the development of legislation and regulations to strengthen waste management practices and reduce sectoral emissions.

projects.name: Development of project management system in the activities of state bodies
projects.description:
The Government of Kazakhstan is actively working to introduce modern project management approaches required in the new realities. The legislative basis for the implementation of project activities in public administration has been formed. The implementation of the project-network model in public administration is envisaged at three levels: portfolio level – at the level of the Government and the Presidential Administration of the Republic of Kazakhstan; program level – at the level of central and local executive bodies; project level – direct implementation of projects by creating project teams and their activities.
The main aim of the project is to improve the quality of public administration and the extent to which key aspects of project management are embedded in the activities of state bodies.
One of the key objectives of the project is to increase the motivation of project staff to develop professional competencies and introduce best practices in project management and to develop project maturity in the country as a whole.

projects.name: Coordination of the Global Partnership for Action to Eliminate all forms of HIV-related stigma and discrimination
projects.description:
In advancing the Global Partnership for Action to Eliminate HIV-Related Stigma and Discrimination in Kazakhstan, the UNAIDS Country Office demonstrated significant progress through the appointment of a national consultant to drive key initiatives. This consultant played a pivotal role in cultivating collaboration among diverse stakeholders, including the Kazakh Scientific Centre for Dermatology and Infection Diseases under the Ministry of Health, the People Living with HIV community, civil society partners, and national/international organizations. After supporting the process of drafting, UNAIDS facilitated multi-stakeholder meetings to track the implementation of the National Plan against Stigma and Discrimination related to HIV. The consultant's contributions were instrumental in bolstering AIDS service non-governmental organizations, particularly in areas such as advocacy for decriminalization of      HIV transmission/exposure and implementation of      the National Plan against Stigma and Discrimination related to HIV. Notably, in partnership with the Kazakhstan Union of People Living with HIV, the consultant facilitated      two pivotal meetings in Almaty and Astana, convening over 40 participants from AIDS Service NGOs, governmental structures, and national/international organizations. These meetings aimed to establish a unified position among civil society organizations regarding the decriminalization of HIV transmission at the country level, as well as gather support to advocacy from select state authorities, along with a number of preparatory meetings. Furthermore, the consultant played a crucial role in supporting AIDS Service NGOs in contributing to a UN confidential report for Kazakhstan's 2023 review by the Committee against Torture, demonstrating proactive involvement and a commitment to transparency and international cooperation.

Despite these steps, transgender individuals in Kazakhstan continue to face legal barriers, stigma, and discrimination, negatively impacting efforts to end the HIV epidemic. Notable legal obstacles include the prohibition of gender-affirming treatment until the age of 21, sterilization requirements for legal gender recognition, and others. Recognizing the urgency of addressing these challenges, the UNAIDS office played a central role in co-organizing a significant meeting focused on overcoming barriers to accessing HIV services for transgender people. This collaborative effort, in partnership with the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB and Malaria and AlmaTQ, a transgender civil society initiative, drew more than 40 participants, including representatives from NGOs, AIDS Centers, and national/international organizations. Discussions centered on addressing challenges related to HIV-associated stigma and human rights, raising awareness, and fostering collaboration among diverse stakeholders. Additionally, the UNAIDS office provided crucial support in enhancing the capacity of the transgender community to pursue strategic lawsuits with the newly established Constitutional Court of Kazakhstan, aimed at reviewing legal provisions discriminating against transgender people. As a direct outcome of these efforts, legislation concerning legal barriers for transgender people underwent comprehensive analysis, two cases were referred to the Constitutional Court, and notably, a comprehensive Transgender Community Advocacy Strategy for 2023-2026 was successfully developed. These accomplishments underscore the UNAIDS Country Office's unwavering commitment to creating a more inclusive and supportive environment for people affected by HIV-related stigma and discrimination in Kazakhstan.

The 'Let Communities Lead' regional leadership campaign commenced with a dynamic three-day communications training for 10 community leaders across six countries. Focused on honing public speaking and media interaction skills, participants crafted engaging content for the campaign's social media drive in Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Over 10 days, leaders were showcased on Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram, amassing a remarkable total reach exceeding 300,000 views. This success underscores the campaign's efficacy in galvanizing and motivating communities through strategic communication. UNAIDS Kazakhstan, a key contributor to the regional initiative, enriched the UNAIDS Global World AIDS Day campaign with a compelling video showcasing how community groups connect at-risk clients to PrEP in Kazakhstan.
